findings.summary: State is used as a core idea (UI = f(props, state), state lost on remount, key resets state) but is never defined or shown anywhere in the chapter.
findings.evidence: "UI = f(props, state): body is pure, no side effects" on page 1, then "state lands on the wrong row" on page 3 and "New type each render: remount, state lost" on page 5, with no explanation of what state is.
findings.fix: Add one line on page 1, such as "State = data a component remembers between renders (useState); props come from the parent, state is owned by the component", so the later state-loss and key-reset points make sense.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "including", "closing").

findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "attributes", "camelcase").
findings.evidence: Use camelCase attributes: className, htmlFor, onClick, tabIndex; style takes an object: style={{ color: 'red' }}
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The 'Lifting Content Up' section puts two separate ideas (no prop drilling, and passed-in elements not re-rendering) in one bullet.
findings.evidence: Avoids prop drilling. Passed-in elements are not re-rendered when the wrapper's state changes.
findings.fix: Split into two one-line bullets: 'Avoids prop drilling' and 'Elements passed as children are not re-rendered when the wrapper's state changes'.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "forgetting", "triggers").
findings.evidence: Forgetting the key, or putting it on the inner element instead of the one returned by map, triggers the warning and bad diffing
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The cheat-sheet Card example destructures a `title` prop it never uses, which muddles the 'destructure props' rule.
findings.fix: Either render {title} in the returned JSX or destructure only `{ children }`, as on page 4.
